summary: Couch Investor reflects on the sharp market correction, calling it 'max pain' for holders of AI, semiconductor, data-centre and fintech names; his own portfolio went from around 40% up year to date at its peak to flat or down. On the day, Nvidia fell another 6.3%, Micron 10%, AMD close to 9–10% and Broadcom close to 9%, while Google rose 1.7%. He puts the S&P 500's roughly 8.3% decline over 46 days against history: the median correction since 2009 is about 7.6% over 26 days, so this one is longer than typical but far short of 2022's 27.5% over 282 days, and November is down 5.27% so far. He screens 14 holdings on forward P/E, calling several cheap: Oracle at 12.6x, Reddit 13.1x, Uber 16.3x, Netflix on its lowest multiple in about a decade, Nu at 11.7x, and the five hyperscalers at a median of 22x; semiconductor ETF SMH holdings sit at a median 20.3x and a weighted 13.2x. His argument is that the questions now being asked about AI spending and returns on investment should have been asked at all-time highs — the businesses he owns have not deteriorated, guidance still points to growth into 2028, and he would rather buy good businesses at undervalued prices than sell and risk buying back higher. He also expects a 25bp Fed hike in December (92% probability) and notes Google's Gemini leads AI chat share at 83.7%. No explicit directional buy, sell or hold calls are made on any individual ticker.
